Akrafena.fact: One Abrafoo group, and possibly all abrafoo groups, have Abrani, Atano God of Executioners, as their patron deity.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: It is usually their job to protect the wives of the _____
Akrafena.fact: It is usually their job to protect the wives of the Asantehene.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: Akofo Ankobia: The highest rank an _____ swordsman can achieve
Akrafena.fact: Akofo Ankobia: The highest rank an Akan swordsman can achieve. They are the Akanland's special forces.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: They are the _____'s special forces
Akrafena.fact: They are the Akanland's special forces.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: The Ankobia is the oldest, most experienced and best trained of all _____
Akrafena.fact: Akofo Ankobia: The highest rank an Akan swordsman can achieve. The Ankobia is the oldest, most experienced and best trained of all Akofo.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: They served as special forces and bodyguards to the _____
Akrafena.fact: They served as special forces and bodyguards to the Asantehene.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: Unlike the Tɔprɛfoɔ who will only execute condemned criminals or war captives, _____ɔ may kill any random person they encounter in their nightly duties to protect Manhyia Palace
Akrafena.fact: Unlike the Tɔprɛfoɔ who will only execute condemned criminals or war captives, Animosumfoɔ may kill any random person they encounter in their nightly duties to protect Manhyia Palace.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: In the past, they used mpre to whip people aside to clear the way for the _____
Akrafena.fact: In the past, they used mpre to whip people aside to clear the way for the Asantehene. It is said that Asantehene Osei Kwame (1777-1798) married the present Animosumhene's great-great-grandmother, Nana Bema (Ɔheneyere Bema), and they bore two sons, Afriyie Kwame and Owusu Ansa.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: The king made one of them the _____ and created the animosum stool for Nana Bema's family so that they would be in charge of his anadwo sekan (night sword)
Akrafena.fact: The king made one of them the Safohene and created the animosum stool for Nana Bema's family so that they would be in charge of his anadwo sekan (night sword).

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: On those occasions, _____ɔ would show up and when the sitting was over, it was their duty to clear the way or guard Otumfoɔ safely back to his residence and guard the palace throughout the night
Akrafena.fact: On those occasions, Anadwo Sekanfoɔ would show up and when the sitting was over, it was their duty to clear the way or guard Otumfoɔ safely back to his residence and guard the palace throughout the night.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: Only the most skilled and deadly at _____ could join the Animosumfoɔ
Akrafena.fact: Knives and swords were not part of their regalia, which is due to them using Akofena (see Akrafena as a martial art) without weapons. Only the most skilled and deadly at Akofena could join the Animosumfoɔ.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: The custodians brought it from _____ɛ when they realized Nana Ntim Gyakari and Denkyiraman were on the verge of losing the war to Ɔpemsoɔ Osei Tutu and Asanteman
Akrafena.fact: The custodians brought it from Adanse Akrokyerɛ when they realized Nana Ntim Gyakari and Denkyiraman were on the verge of losing the war to Ɔpemsoɔ Osei Tutu and Asanteman.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: Because they belong to the Asona clan, they first went to _____, Akwamuhene at that time, who later took them to formally introduce them to Ɔpemsoɔ Osei Tutu
Akrafena.fact: Because they belong to the Asona clan, they first went to Nana Oti Awere, Akwamuhene at that time, who later took them to formally introduce them to Ɔpemsoɔ Osei Tutu.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: Osei Tutu then asked the _____ at the time, Nana Agyeibi, to give them a place
Akrafena.fact: Osei Tutu then asked the Atwemahene at the time, Nana Agyeibi, to give them a place.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: The king later created a stool and a chief for them and gave them the kantankrakyi sword and ordered them to use it as part of the regalia that protects _____
Akrafena.fact: The king later created a stool and a chief for them and gave them the kantankrakyi sword and ordered them to use it as part of the regalia that protects Sikadwa Kofi.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: The story is told of _____ who came upon the atoprɛ drum in the forest on one of his hunting expeditions
Akrafena.fact: The story is told of Nana Gyamanin Awere who came upon the atoprɛ drum in the forest on one of his hunting expeditions.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: Since they did not know the name of the drum, who owned it, or what it was used for, _____ consulted the family's deity, Ɔworɔ
Akrafena.fact: The story is told of Nana Gyamanin Awere who came upon the atoprɛ drum in the forest on one of his hunting expeditions. Since they did not know the name of the drum, who owned it, or what it was used for, Gyamanin Awere consulted the family's deity, Ɔworɔ.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: The priest went on to say that _____'s family would perish if they decided to keep the drum
Akrafena.fact: The priest went on to say that Nana Gyamanin Awere's family would perish if they decided to keep the drum.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: The only time the drum is played is on _____ɔda (the Monday after Akwasidae when they are in the process of executing a criminal)
Akrafena.fact: The only time the drum is played is on Akwasidae Dwoɔda (the Monday after Akwasidae when they are in the process of executing a criminal).

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: As the Akan saying goes, Atoprɛ to a etwa Dwoɔda (Atɔprɛ takes place on _____)
Akrafena.fact: The only time the drum is played is on Akwasidae Dwoɔda (the Monday after Akwasidae when they are in the process of executing a criminal). As the Akan saying goes, Atoprɛ to a etwa Dwoɔda (Atɔprɛ takes place on Monday).

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: “_____ you seen your ear before?” They would cut his ear and show it to him
Akrafena.fact: When the convict was paraded in the streets, they would, for instance, ask him, “have you seen the skin on your back before?” Then they would cut the skin on his back and show it to him. “Have you seen your ear before?” They would cut his ear and show it to him.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: One of the most famous of his nephews was _____ and that gave rise to the saying: Anin Agyei a odi atɔfoɔ kan (Anin Agyei who leads the condemned)
Akrafena.fact: One of the most famous of his nephews was Anin Agyei and that gave rise to the saying: Anin Agyei a odi atɔfoɔ kan (Anin Agyei who leads the condemned).

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: This would continue until they returned to the palace where the _____ would confirm and congratulate them for performing atoprɛ
Akrafena.fact: This would continue until they returned to the palace where the Asantehene would confirm and congratulate them for performing atoprɛ.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: Because the chief's hand would be covered with human blood, he would not shake _____ɔ's hand
Akrafena.fact: Because the chief's hand would be covered with human blood, he would not shake Otumfoɔ's hand. The condemned person was not allowed be killed nor should he pass away until he is presented in his mutilated and bleeding state to Otumfoɔ.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: The condemned person was not allowed be killed nor should he pass away until he is presented in his mutilated and bleeding state to _____ɔ
Akrafena.fact: Because the chief's hand would be covered with human blood, he would not shake Otumfoɔ's hand. The condemned person was not allowed be killed nor should he pass away until he is presented in his mutilated and bleeding state to Otumfoɔ.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: Function: They are always available to protect Abenwa (the _____) and in the absence of Abenwa, they protect Otumfoɔ's akonwa (chair) during akwasidae ceremonies or dwabɔ
Akrafena.fact: Function: They are always available to protect Abenwa (the Gold Stool) and in the absence of Abenwa, they protect Otumfoɔ's akonwa (chair) during akwasidae ceremonies or dwabɔ.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: In this context it is known as _____
Akrafena.fact: In this context it is called Akofena.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: Nsuaefena is used in the political ceremony of taking the oath of office by the king and in the swearing oaths of allegiance by subjects of _____-State
Akrafena.fact: Nsuaefena is used in the political ceremony of taking the oath of office by the king and in the swearing oaths of allegiance by subjects of Ashanti City-State. The akrafena also may be carried as a heraldic device, by the Ashanti emperor's-king's emissaries on Ashanti City-State diplomatic missions.

Akrafena.question: The first _____ akfrafena sword was created by Asantehene Nana Opoku Ware I (r
Akrafena.fact: The Ashanti national symbol akrafena description: The Akrafena is a prominent symbol of the Ashantis in the 18th, 19th and 20th centuries into the 21st century The akrafena as an Ashanti national symbol has the escutcheon meaning Akrafena ("Symbol of courage, valor, and heroism"). The Omanhene used the Ashanti akrafena to swear the oath of allegiance to the Asantehene and Ashanti City-State.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: _____ – 1742), and is the foremost example of akrafena
Akrafena.fact: 1731 – 1742), and is the foremost example of akrafena.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: The mpomponsuo sword symbolizes _____, Power, Loyalty, Bravery, and Authority
Akrafena.fact: There is a hierarchy when it comes to akrafena (not Bosomfena) in Asante court: Mpomponsuo: The Mpomponsuo sword symbolizes; Responsibility, Power, Loyalty, Bravery, and Authority.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: The schools hold the genuine _____ sword techniques
Akrafena.fact: The first Ashanti akfrafena sword was created by Asantehene Nana Opoku Ware I (r. The schools hold the genuine Ashanti sword techniques.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: The sword-based fighting techniques is similar in part to that of _____ grima and Tire machèt, while the combat hand-techniques and kicking techniques are similar in part to that of capoeira
Akrafena.fact: The sword-based fighting techniques is similar in part to that of Colombian grima and Tire machèt, while the combat hand-techniques and kicking techniques are similar in part to that of capoeira.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: At any rate, _____ worked tirelessly and was determined to restore the kingdom but he died in 1931 before he could accomplish his goal
Akrafena.fact: At any rate, Nana Agyeman Prempeh worked tirelessly and was determined to restore the kingdom but he died in 1931 before he could accomplish his goal.

Akrafena.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Akrafena.question: On assumption of office in 1931, _____ II embarked on this difficult task and eventually succeeded in restoring the Asante State in 1935
Akrafena.fact: On assumption of office in 1931, Agyemang Prempeh II embarked on this difficult task and eventually succeeded in restoring the Asante State in 1935.
